investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-18T22:33–22:40Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner collected zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~143–147 s), preventing VM provisioning and causing all downstream contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in [running,idle,ready]) to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or scheduling constraint failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval layer.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both nodes that carry the kata peer-pods VM resource are fully allocated, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption is also unavailable, confirming no lower-priority pods can be evicted.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the four remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, which may indicate a labeling change, node replacement, or taint that removed previously eligible nodes from the schedulable pool, effectively reducing capacity from a larger set to only 2 nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval runs: if multiple eval runs or real workloads are competing for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion could occur without a permanent capacity deficit.

Lower confidence — node affinity selector in the remote-agent pod spec may be overly restrictive, preventing the scheduler from considering nodes that could otherwise host the workload even without the kata.peerpods.io/vm label.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T22:38–22:40Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remained unscheduled for ~147 seconds until the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints, and preemption found no victims to evict. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during this eval window was rejected by the scheduler, preventing agent creation and causing all downstream checks (state, runtime) to fail with empty evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state all reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm'.
